title: Preethi Eco Plus Mixer Grinder 110-Volt for use in USA/Canada, white, 3-jar
description:
About this item
The Preethi ECO PLUS MG-138 Mixer Grinder features 550 Watt motor. The mixer comes with 100% stainless steel jars with flow breakers for fine grinding.
The steel blades of the mixer grinder are machine ground and polished for maximum grinding efficiency.
It has high grade Nylon Couplers for smooth and hassle free operation. The clear and transparent polycarbonate domes & lids add to the quality factor. The sturdy handles are ergonomically designed.
Comes with 3 (1.5 Liter, 1.0 Liter and 0.4 Liter) Stainless steel Jars for Wet and Dry grinding, whipping, churning Grating, Mincing, and Chopping
Please user manual under the product details for setup and usage related guidance.

Love this one! Perfect for Indian cookingI was looking for a blender in the US for daily smoothies and occasional chutney, pesto, hummus, or spice grinding. American blenders all have plastic jars and only single jars, so I chose this Preethi mixie for its 3 different steel jars. I've been satisfied for this first month of daily use.
-- 5 stars: For daily smoothies using frozen or fresh fruit, spinach and yogurt, I found the large jar grinds to a smooth creamy consistency whereas the middle jar leaves visible bits of spinach. The middle jar is better for chutney rather than creamy smoothies. The large jar also works great for hummus.
-- 5 stars: The small jar works great for masalas or coffee beans. But you need to use enough to reach the blades. It won't work for tiny amounts.
-- 3 stars: This model is only 500W which is not very strong for a blender or mixie, so I thaw the chunky frozen fruit first. I find I have to run it for a long time to get things to grind fully and not leave lumps. I even sometimes set the timer for 2 or 3 minutes and stand there (because the lids don't latch). But it does eventually grind things to a very fine or creamy consistency.
-- Five stars: It came with several replacement parts and a tool to loosen the bottom of the jars. I haven't used any of those yet but I really appreciate that they came with it. With previous mixies I broke the plastic gear teeth by trying to grind jaggery chunks, and I had to take it to a dealer to replace the bottom of the jar. That was in India and cost a couple hundred rupees in 10 minutes, but would be impossible or expensive here in the US, for any model of blender/mixie.After my parents moved from India to the US, they were dissatisfied with all the grinders I bought for them, including Ninja and NutriBullet models. They wanted something familiar, so I got the Preethi Mixer.

This mixer is incredibly loud, but my parents are happy with it. Although you can buy it from some import websites for 40% cheaper, I chose to purchase it through Amazon for the comfort of their return policy, despite the higher cost.

Overall, it’s a reliable option if you're looking for a familiar, effective mixer, but be prepared for the noise.A must buy for indian kitchens. Preethi is available is USA and works well. Major drawbacks:

Flawed Lids: A critical shortcoming of this appliance is the poorly designed lids. Made from transparent polycarbonate, these lids reportedly don't secure properly, causing a mess in the kitchen as food splatters or spills out during grinding. This not only makes for a frustrating user experience but also necessitates extra cleaning after every use.

Questionable Durability: The construction of the Preethi Eco Plus raises concerns about long-term use. The plastic base, while seemingly lightweight, might not be the most robust choice for a kitchen appliance. Additionally, the reliance on high-grade nylon couplers is a potential point of failure. Nylon, while suitable for some applications, can degrade over time and become brittle, potentially leading to breakdowns and repairs.

In summary, while the Preethi Eco Plus Mixer Grinder might seem appealing at first glance due to its motor power and stainless steel jars, the significant issues with the lids and the potentially problematic use of plastic and nylon couplers make it a questionable purchase. Users are likely to encounter frustration and mess due to the faulty lids, and the long-term durability remains uncertain.
